title: The Moth Who Taxed the Moon
story: Every full moon, Lanternquist the Tithe Moth settles on the silk-weavers' roof and demands a cut of their moonsilk before she'll let the looms turn. Tonight the weavers have spun 240 skeins, and the moth announces she will take 35% of them — plus an extra 12 skeins as a 'landing fee.' Mr 6 climbs the roof beam, sword sheathed, abacus out, because this moth can be beaten by arithmetic alone.
question: If Lanternquist takes 35% of the 240 skeins plus 12 more, how many skeins are left for the weavers?
solution: The moth's total take is 84 + 12 = 96 skeins.
240 - 96 = 144 skeins are left for the weavers.
praise: Finding 35% of 240 was exactly the right opening move — the landing fee of 12 just needed to join the pile before you subtracted.
hint: First work out 35% of 240. Then remember the moth asks for 12 MORE on top of that before you subtract from 240.
victory: Mr 6 read the tally aloud so clearly that Lanternquist realized her 'landing fee' had been double-counted for years, and she fluttered off red-winged with apologies. The looms clattered back to life before midnight.
imagePrompt: A huge pale moth with ledger-marks on her wings perched on a moonlit weaving-house roof, silver skeins glowing below, while a small knightly numeral 6 in a blue cape holds up a tally board.
